Released on 2026-11-05. Barn 1.0.0 is the first stable release. GitHub's
`releases/latest`, the download installer without `BARN_VERSION`, and the
Homebrew formula select it.

Barn 1.0.0 finishes a pre-release audit of destructive operations, data-disk
recovery, catalog integrity, and process cancellation. It embeds signed image
catalog revision `2026110502`, including Debian 13 image `20261103.2651.1` for
amd64 and arm64.

## Changes

- **Safer whole-deployment recreate.** A `recreate` without node selectors
  refuses an inventory that no longer lists an existing node (`conflict`,
  reason `nodes_removed`, exit 4) before any VM stops; earlier releases
  destroyed the omitted node without recreating it. Remove a node explicitly
  with `barn destroy NODE` or add it back to the inventory. The confirmation
  lists every node the operation replaces, and the scope is checked again
  under the destruction lock (`deployment_changed` when the applied state
  changed during preflight).
- **Destroying the control node keeps the lab usable.** The first remaining
  node becomes the control node, with a consistent state, so `ssh-config`,
  `hosts`, `exec`, and `provision` keep working. Update the inventory's control
  role, then run `barn up` to install its control SSH access. Barn refuses to
  destroy the control node, before deleting anything, when the successor has an
  unfinished prepare record that cannot be completed.
- **Data disks are reset only on recognized corruption.** Disks with a
  partition table, a signature without a UUID, unsupported filesystem
  features, or an unknown checker failure keep their data and report a
  warning. An ext4 or XFS filesystem is reset only after the checker reports
  recognized corruption. Existing guests receive the updated helper on their
  next `barn up` readiness check.
- **Confirmations.**
  - On a terminal, `up`, `start`, `restart`, and `reload` show the
    host-preparation plan and ask once before installing packages or the Barn
    network, as `barn setup` does. Without a terminal they still only report
    what is missing; run `barn setup --yes` for unattended preparation.
  - `destroy`, `recreate`, `mac destroy`, and `mac recreate` accept `--yes` as
    their confirmation flag. `--force` keeps working, and `mac stop --force`
    still powers the VM off.
- **Catalog integrity has its own exit code.** A catalog signature or signed
  revision that does not verify exits 7 (`integrity`, reason
  `catalog_signature` or `catalog_equivocation`) instead of 1. Permission and
  I/O errors on a cached signature remain runtime failures (exit 1). Both
  official repositories share the embedded upgrade baseline, a new trusted
  signature over identical catalog bytes is accepted, and catalog commands keep
  working after `barn image reset` on an earlier version followed by an
  upgrade.
- **Cancellation reaches `sudo`.** Cancelled commands receive SIGTERM, which
  `sudo` forwards, and Barn waits at most 10 seconds for the process and its
  inherited pipes. Descendants that ignore SIGTERM still need external
  supervision.
- **Host networking and Mac images.** `barn network uninstall` keeps the
  global networkd unit state when other host links exist or exclusive Barn use
  cannot be established; the plan reports `preserve_networkd` and the applied
  report explains the decision in `checks.networkd`. Mac image pruning keeps
  bases referenced by interrupted recreates; a malformed recovery journal stops
  the cleanup until its references are known.
- **CLI.**
  - Running `barn` without a command prints the complete help, as
    `barn --help` does; `--json` and `--yaml` keep the `actions[]` document.
  - Explicit `--json`/`--yaml` and `--verbose` override `BARN_OUTPUT` and
    `BARN_VERBOSE`, and help stays available when those variables are invalid.
- **Dependencies.** Go 1.27.3, `golang.org/x/net` 0.62.0, and
  `go.yaml.in/yaml/v3` 3.0.6.

## Upgrade

The installer selects the latest stable release, verifies the archive against
the release's `checksums.txt`, and installs into `~/.local/bin` without sudo:

```bash
curl -fLO https://github.com/pgsty/barn/releases/latest/download/install.sh
bash install.sh
```

Set `BARN_VERSION=1.0.0` to pin this release. On macOS, run
`brew upgrade barn` (or `brew install pgsty/infra/barn`). On Linux, install the
DEB or RPM package from the release.

Upgrading from 0.9.3 requires no recreation; VM disks, SSH keys, state, and
configuration stay under `~/.barn`. Stop macOS VMs before replacing the native
component. Check scripts for these changes:

- catalog signature failures now exit 7 instead of 1;
- a whole-deployment `recreate` exits 4 when the inventory omits an existing
  node;
- interactive `up` asks before preparing the host.

The Apple Silicon archive and Homebrew installation include the signed,
notarized `Barn.app`, CLI, and hosts helper. Linux arm64/amd64 and Intel macOS
provide the CLI and hosts helper; Linux guests use QEMU.

## Known limitations

- A malformed Mac recovery journal stops `barn mac image ls`, the space
  estimate in `barn mac doctor`, and image pruning until it is repaired.
- One unreadable Mac machine state stops listing all machines; machines are
  still usable by name.
- Linux guest shares on macOS hosts need a guest kernel with 9p support.

## Support

Security fixes land in the latest 1.x patch release. 0.x releases receive no
further fixes; upgrade to 1.0.0. See
[SECURITY.md](https://github.com/pgsty/barn/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

See the [installation guide](https://barn.pgsty.com/docs/start/installation/),
the [Linux quick start](https://barn.pgsty.com/docs/start/tutorial/), and the
[Mac guide](https://barn.pgsty.com/docs/start/macos/).
